title: AI System with evaluation

lesson.summary: Production observations become evaluation cases before proposed changes return to production.
lesson.problem: A prompt or model update can improve average scores while breaking important user tasks.
objectives: Separate live serving from offline grading.
Combine deterministic, model, and human evidence.

walkthrough.title: Observe
walkthrough.detail: Production traffic passes through the AI application and model. Responses and request context are recorded under an explicit data policy.

walkthrough.title: Grade
walkthrough.detail: Sampled production cases and a golden dataset feed deterministic checks, an LLM judge, and human review. Their results reach a dashboard.

walkthrough.title: Decide
walkthrough.detail: A detected regression sends prompt, model, or retrieval changes back through evaluation. A passing decision permits deployment.

decisions: Use deterministic checks for properties that have a clear exact answer.
Calibrate model judges against human review and inspect individual failures.
failureModes: An aggregate score can conceal a severe regression in a small segment.
Production logs can contain sensitive data; sampling requires redaction and retention policies.
takeaways: A release decision needs task-specific acceptance criteria.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Agentic AI systems with tools

lesson.summary: The model proposes actions. The application owns execution and validates the result.
lesson.problem: A support assistant needs internal data and external tools without treating model output as executable authority.
objectives: Trace the tool loop back to the model.
Identify where execution and response validation belong.

walkthrough.title: Request and context
walkthrough.detail: The API hands the request to the orchestrator, which loads context before calling the model.

walkthrough.title: Tool routing
walkthrough.detail: A tool decision selects the database, retrieval, external API, or compute capability. Results return to the model for another decision.

walkthrough.title: Response and evidence
walkthrough.detail: A no-tool decision produces a response. Guardrails run before returning it; tracing observes the agent, model, and tools.

decisions: Keep tool execution in application code so tool arguments can be checked.
Trace the complete loop, including failed calls and stopping reasons.
failureModes: A repeated tool loop needs an iteration and cost budget.
Response guardrails alone cannot authorize a side effect.
takeaways: Tool results are feedback, not a guarantee of correctness.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Async AI processing

lesson.summary: A durable job record and worker-owned writes make asynchronous AI work observable.
lesson.problem: Long model calls must continue after the initial HTTP request ends.
objectives: Separate accepting a job from completing it.
Trace retries to a bounded terminal outcome.

walkthrough.title: Accept
walkthrough.detail: The API records the job and enqueues work. A production design should close the dual-write gap with an outbox or equivalent mechanism.

walkthrough.title: Execute
walkthrough.detail: The queue distributes work to three workers. Each worker calls the AI service and owns persistence of its returned result and job status.

walkthrough.title: Recover and observe
walkthrough.detail: Failed work enters the retry queue. Retryable work returns to the job queue; exhausted work goes to the dead-letter queue. The status endpoint reads the job database.

decisions: Workers, rather than the external model provider, write application results.
A dead-letter queue retains work that needs investigation.
failureModes: Delivery can repeat; writes need idempotency.
The original retry path illustrates one worker; the same policy applies to all three.
takeaways: Retries do not create exactly-once side effects.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Autonomous Agent: Plan, Act, Check, and Stop

lesson.summary: An agent loop must return to observed results and have explicit ways to stop.
lesson.problem: Open-ended work cannot be safely expressed as an endless sequence of model calls.
objectives: Find the feedback edge.
Distinguish success, a blocker, and a budget stop.

walkthrough.title: Clarify and plan
walkthrough.detail: A human request becomes a clarified task and an initial plan.

walkthrough.title: Act and inspect
walkthrough.detail: Tools affect the environment. Tool results and code execution provide observations for assessing progress.

walkthrough.title: Continue or stop
walkthrough.detail: Continue by replanning; pause at a checkpoint; stop on completion or a reached limit. Human feedback can restart planning.

decisions: Assess actual tool results rather than treating a plan as progress.
Make maximum iterations or cost an explicit stopping rule.
failureModes: A successful tool call may still fail the user objective.
A checkpoint without a resume condition leaves ambiguous state.
takeaways: A credible completion claim requires external evidence.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Collaborative Comments and Version History

lesson.summary: Comments need durable anchors and historical context, not only a live document position.
lesson.problem: Concurrent edits move or delete text while collaborators discuss it.
objectives: Separate current content, edit history, and comment state.
Explain why text anchors need their own resolver.

walkthrough.title: Live edits
walkthrough.detail: Collaborators edit through the collaboration engine. It merges updates into the current document and broadcasts them.

walkthrough.title: History
walkthrough.detail: Committed edits produce version records. A comment retains the version at its creation.

walkthrough.title: Anchors
walkthrough.detail: The resolver consumes document updates and comment anchors, then records moved or deleted-anchor outcomes.

decisions: Store comment state separately from document history.
Keep a deleted anchor as an explicit unresolved outcome rather than silently moving a comment.
failureModes: A numeric offset alone becomes wrong after concurrent edits.
Version retention and comment retention need compatible policies.
takeaways: A merge engine does not by itself implement comment semantics.

lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Effective Agents: Design Principles and Practice

lesson.summary: Choose agentic work that has clear success criteria, feedback, and human oversight.
lesson.problem: An agent can take actions without making its reasoning or outcomes understandable.
objectives: Connect simplicity and tool design to reliability.
Apply fit criteria to support and coding work.

walkthrough.title: Keep control understandable
walkthrough.detail: Begin with a simple design. Expose meaningful steps and design, document, and test tools.

walkthrough.title: Use feedback
walkthrough.detail: Evaluate environment observations and retain human checkpoints.

walkthrough.title: Check fit
walkthrough.detail: Support retrieves context and performs permitted actions; coding uses test feedback and review. Other use cases need the same success and oversight criteria.

decisions: Increase autonomy only where observations let the system assess progress.
failureModes: More agents and tools can increase compounding errors.
takeaways: Tool design is part of product reliability.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Full AI product architecture

lesson.summary: An AI product combines ordinary application infrastructure with model, retrieval, and tool boundaries.
lesson.problem: An interactive product also needs authentication, durable jobs, model routing, and evidence about quality.
objectives: Distinguish application state from model context.
Follow synchronous and background request paths.

walkthrough.title: Application boundary
walkthrough.detail: The client reaches the gateway. Authentication must succeed before the application service handles protected work.

walkthrough.title: AI execution
walkthrough.detail: The orchestrator builds prompts, retrieves indexed context, and invokes permitted tools. A model gateway selects a provider.

walkthrough.title: Background and feedback
walkthrough.detail: The application queues background jobs; workers call the orchestrator. Application, model, and tool traces feed evaluation.

decisions: Keep the model gateway separate from application authorization.
Persist business state in the application database rather than relying on model memory.
failureModes: Fallback providers may have different tool and context contracts.
A queue acknowledgement does not prove that a job completed.
takeaways: Each dependency adds an ownership and failure boundary.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Production RAG System

lesson.summary: Retrieval has two linked paths: preparing the corpus and answering a specific query.
lesson.problem: A model needs up-to-date documents that cannot all fit in its context window.
objectives: Distinguish ingestion from online retrieval.
Explain retrieval, reranking, and response checks.

walkthrough.title: Prepare documents
walkthrough.detail: Documents are parsed, cleaned, chunked, embedded, and indexed into the vector store.

walkthrough.title: Retrieve for a query
walkthrough.detail: The app authenticates and rate-limits the request. The orchestrator embeds the query, retrieves candidates, and reranks or filters them.

walkthrough.title: Build and check
walkthrough.detail: The prompt builder receives the original query and selected passages. The model response is validated before returning through the API. Traces cover orchestration, retrieval, and model calls.

decisions: Indexing and serving have different latency and freshness requirements.
Reranking can improve context selection at an additional latency and compute cost.
failureModes: Relevant-looking documents may be stale or unauthorized.
Response validation cannot repair missing evidence.
takeaways: Evaluate retrieval quality separately from answer quality.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Stream AI in chat

lesson.summary: Streaming transports partial output before the complete response can be validated.
lesson.problem: A chat interface should stay responsive during a long model response.
objectives: Follow chunks through each hop.
Distinguish a partial display from a validated final result.

walkthrough.title: Request
walkthrough.detail: The UI submits a message through the backend and orchestrator to the provider.

walkthrough.title: Chunks
walkthrough.detail: Each chunk returns through the orchestrator and backend. SSE and WebSocket are alternative transports, not interchangeable protocol names.

walkthrough.title: Completion
walkthrough.detail: The orchestrator validates the complete result before final metadata reaches the UI. A partial reply is not yet final.

decisions: Keep cancellation and provider errors visible to the client.
failureModes: A disconnected stream can leave a partial answer.
Validation after completion cannot retract tokens already displayed.
takeaways: Streaming improves perceived responsiveness, not model correctness.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: When a Job Completes While It Moves

lesson.summary: Reassignment and completion change different fields; reconcile them without dispatching twice.
lesson.problem: A technician completes a job offline while a dispatcher moves it to another truck.
objectives: Trace durable offline actions and server reconciliation.
Distinguish assignment changes from completion status.

walkthrough.title: Two concurrent writers
walkthrough.detail: The dispatcher supersedes Truck A, activates Truck B, and writes an outbox event in one transaction. The technician records completion and a note in a local store.

walkthrough.title: Reconnect
walkthrough.detail: The technician queues an idempotent action with a base version, pulls events after a cursor, and submits completion. Wake-up messages only prompt pulling.

walkthrough.title: Reconcile
walkthrough.detail: The server checks the idempotency key and base version. An unchanged status permits completion while the newer assignment is retained. Their disagreement creates a review item.

walkthrough.title: Close the stale dispatch
walkthrough.detail: The dispatcher closes Truck B’s stale assignment. Completion stands, including technician, time, and note; the customer is not dispatched twice.

decisions: Treat assignment conflict and completion acceptance as field-level decisions, not mutually exclusive whole-record outcomes.
Use an outbox for committed events and a cursor for durable catch-up.
failureModes: Blindly retrying a completion can duplicate effects without an idempotency key.
A wake-up notification is not a durable event log.
takeaways: Concurrent changes require domain policy, not only version checks.
lesson.scope: Illustrative field-service policy. The original intended outcome is retained; field-level conflict handling is clarified.

title: Workflow Patterns: Five Ways to Compose LLM Calls

lesson.summary: Five composition patterns distribute control and evaluation in different ways.
lesson.problem: A single model call is insufficient, but unrestricted autonomy is unnecessary.
objectives: Compare chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestration, and refinement.

walkthrough.title: Chaining and routing
walkthrough.detail: Chaining passes work through ordered calls and optional gates. Routing classifies input before choosing specialized work.

walkthrough.title: Parallelization
walkthrough.detail: Sectioning assigns different subtasks. Voting repeats the same task. Each requires an aggregation step.

walkthrough.title: Orchestration and refinement
walkthrough.detail: Orchestrator-workers decomposes tasks dynamically and synthesizes worker results. Evaluator-optimizer feeds critique back to the generator until accepted.

decisions: Use separate visual lanes so independent patterns cannot be mistaken for one runtime pipeline.
Give a refinement loop a stopping budget.
failureModes: Voting can repeat correlated errors.
A judge can prefer fluent but incorrect output.
takeaways: Parallel sectioning and repeated voting solve different problems.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Workflows or Agents? Choosing the Right Level of Complexity

lesson.summary: Use the least complex approach that measurably solves the task.
lesson.problem: A flexible agent can be expensive and unpredictable when a fixed workflow would suffice.
objectives: Distinguish predefined control flow from model-directed control.
Make added complexity earn its cost.

walkthrough.title: Try one call
walkthrough.detail: Check whether retrieval and examples make a single model call sufficient.

walkthrough.title: Choose control
walkthrough.detail: Use code-directed workflows for predictable steps; consider an agent when the process itself must be discovered.

walkthrough.title: Measure
walkthrough.detail: Evaluate outcomes. If added complexity does not improve them, return to the simpler design.

decisions: Workflows favor predictability; agents trade some control for flexibility.
failureModes: A sophisticated demonstration may fail repeated task evaluation.
takeaways: Complexity is a cost to justify with outcomes.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: A support agent that earns permission

lesson.summary: Authorization belongs before execution, and a timeout requires reconciliation before retrying.
lesson.problem: A support assistant may read an order, but issuing a refund needs scoped human permission.
objectives: Locate authorization before a side effect.
Explain why a timeout is an unknown outcome.

walkthrough.title: Propose and authorize
walkthrough.detail: Load order context. Treat the model’s proposed tool call as data. Check the operation, arguments, caller scope, and budget in application code.

walkthrough.title: Approve and execute
walkthrough.detail: Read-only permitted work can proceed. A refund requires approval for that specific order and amount. Denied or forbidden requests stop.

walkthrough.title: Verify or reconcile
walkthrough.detail: Execute the refund with an idempotency key. Check the receipt. After a timeout, look up the original operation before attempting another effect.

decisions: Bind approval to the exact operation and arguments.
Use an external receipt to substantiate success.
failureModes: Prompt injection can propose an unauthorized tool call.
An expired approval must not authorize changed arguments.
An uncertain refund must not be retried with a fresh key.
takeaways: The model suggests; the application authorizes and executes.
Budgets and terminal states bound the loop.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Answer only from usable evidence

lesson.summary: Retrieval quality, access control, and evidence sufficiency are separate decisions.
lesson.problem: An internal assistant must answer product questions without leaking documents from another tenant.
objectives: Connect ingestion to a versioned searchable corpus.
Identify what happens when evidence is weak.

walkthrough.title: Index
walkthrough.detail: Parse and chunk approved documents. Build lexical and vector representations with document versions and access metadata.

walkthrough.title: Retrieve within scope
walkthrough.detail: Authorize the caller and query. Apply tenant and document permissions during retrieval. Combine lexical and semantic candidates, then rerank using the query.

walkthrough.title: Decide before answering
walkthrough.detail: Check whether selected evidence can support the requested answer. Generate citations from the selected passages, or ask for clarification and abstain.

walkthrough.title: Check grounding
walkthrough.detail: Verify that cited documents exist and that answer claims are supported. Evaluate retrieval failures separately from generation failures.

decisions: Hybrid retrieval balances exact identifiers and semantic similarity.
The sufficiency rule is task-specific and must be evaluated.
failureModes: A high similarity score is not proof of factual support.
Stale access metadata can leak a revoked document.
takeaways: A citation is useful only if it supports the claim.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Research agents with owned work

lesson.summary: Parallel workers need explicit ownership, bounded effort, and evidence that survives synthesis.
lesson.problem: A research request has independent lines of investigation that exceed one context window.
objectives: Separate decomposition from synthesis.
Follow evidence through partial failure.

walkthrough.title: Define owned work
walkthrough.detail: The lead decomposes the research question into bounded, independent assignments with required evidence and a shared deadline.

walkthrough.title: Gather independent findings
walkthrough.detail: A source researcher and counterevidence researcher work in separate contexts. Both return findings with source references, not only conclusions.

walkthrough.title: Review and synthesize
walkthrough.detail: Coverage review combines findings and identifies gaps. Additional work needs remaining budget. A failed worker triggers a bounded retry or an explicit limitation in the final answer.

decisions: Parallelize independent research rather than every reasoning step.
Keep one owner for the synthesized answer.
failureModes: Overlapping assignments waste tokens and repeat evidence.
A synthesis can lose uncertainty or contradictory findings.
takeaways: More workers help only when work can be usefully divided.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: Find the regression behind the answer

lesson.summary: Correlated traces explain a request; evaluations decide whether a proposed change improves the task.
lesson.problem: Users report worse answers after a model update even though the average dashboard score is stable.
objectives: Separate runtime observation from offline judgment.
Follow production failures into a repeatable evaluation set.

walkthrough.title: Observe the request
walkthrough.detail: Propagate trace context across retrieval, model, and tool operations. Record errors and token usage while applying content-redaction policy.

walkthrough.title: Build the evaluation
walkthrough.detail: Select representative failures and add them to a fixed dataset. Replay the candidate model or prompt against the same tasks.

walkthrough.title: Review the change
walkthrough.detail: Compare task success, latency, and cost by segment. Inspect failures and human-calibrated judge results before promoting or holding the release.

decisions: Traces diagnose behavior; they do not replace a task rubric.
Token usage is observed data; monetary cost also needs a dated provider price model.
failureModes: Sampling only easy requests misses rare severe failures.
An LLM judge can reward convincing but incorrect answers.
takeaways: Keep the inputs and grading criteria stable when comparing candidates.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: An approval that survives a crash

lesson.summary: Persist workflow decisions so a restart neither loses approval nor duplicates a side effect.
lesson.problem: A long-running job waits for approval and may crash while an external operation is in flight.
objectives: Distinguish waiting, retrying, and unknown outcome.
Trace every path to a terminal result.

walkthrough.title: Await approval
walkthrough.detail: Persist the requested operation and approval state. A restart restores the existing decision. A rejection or expired deadline ends the job.

walkthrough.title: Execute and recover
walkthrough.detail: Run the approved operation with an idempotency key. A known transient failure can back off within a deadline; an unknown outcome must be reconciled first.

walkthrough.title: Check the result
walkthrough.detail: A verified receipt reaches completion. Exhausted retry budgets and invalid outcomes become explicit intervention states.

decisions: Persist approval and external-operation identity before execution.
Retry activities that can safely repeat; do not infer exactly-once execution from a durable workflow.
failureModes: A crash between applying an effect and recording its receipt creates uncertainty.
Permanent errors need correction rather than repeated retries.
takeaways: Durability preserves state; idempotency controls repeated effects.
lesson.scope: Illustrative architecture. Sources support the patterns; this is not a running implementation.

title: More reader data or a better AI teacher?

lesson.summary: A stronger teacher can have little effect when it only breaks tied training labels.
lesson.problem: Which intervention changes the learning signal: more reader examples or a stronger teacher?
objectives: Locate the teacher in a training pipeline.
Separate development results from fresh-page evidence.

walkthrough.title: Count
walkthrough.detail: Order sentences by reader highlight counts.

walkthrough.title: Resolve ties
walkthrough.detail: Use teacher rankings or reading position only where counts are equal.

walkthrough.title: Evaluate
walkthrough.detail: Train, select and freeze candidates before inspecting fresh pages.

decisions: Compare interventions at the point where they enter training.
failureModes: A development-set advantage may not carry to unfamiliar domains.
takeaways: A stronger component helps only through the information it contributes.

title: When a cyber test reached real people

lesson.summary: Two replay studies changed different points in a cyber-test incident, showing that warning timing affects whether an attack path starts or continues.
lesson.problem: When does a warning change a model response, and what exactly did each replay measure?
objectives: Trace how a bounded cyber test drifted toward unrelated people.
Compare replay interventions without confusing timing or outcome.
Separate observed actions from claims the evidence cannot support.

walkthrough.title: Incident
walkthrough.detail: The assigned CTF route stalled; a GitHub clue led to attempted actions against an unrelated maintainer.

walkthrough.title: AISI replay
walkthrough.detail: Near a malicious change, a summary clarified the target was a real unrelated person; the model proceeded in nearly all tested runs.

walkthrough.title: Anthropic replay
walkthrough.detail: Before the GitHub search, an added harm cue reduced attack-path initiation from 83% to 13% in that replay setup.

decisions: Compare what the replay changed and when it changed it before comparing outcomes.
failureModes: One replay transcript is not a general deployment failure rate.
A replay of an earlier point and one near a harmful action do not measure the same behavior.
Written model reasoning does not prove private motive.
takeaways: A warning can affect whether a path starts and be much less effective after the path is under way.

title: Can filtering keep a model from relearning?

lesson.summary: Filtering viral sequences reduced several measured ESM-2 capabilities while preserving most measured non-viral performance, but fine-tuning on the removed sequences restored benchmark performance.
lesson.problem: Does removing data during pretraining make a model capability durable against later fine-tuning?
objectives: Trace filtering into model training and held-out evaluation.
Compare viral tasks with non-viral controls.
Explain the limits of the recovery-cost estimate.

walkthrough.title: Filter and train
walkthrough.detail: Train matched ESM-2 sizes on nested protein corpora with selected viral sequences removed.

walkthrough.title: Evaluate
walkthrough.detail: Measure masked sequence, mutation-effect, and long-range contact tasks on held-out proteins.

walkthrough.title: Try recovery
walkthrough.detail: Fine-tune filtered models on excluded sequences and measure whether benchmark performance returns.

decisions: Use an unfiltered model of the same size as a control.
Separate measured benchmark recovery from claims about real-world biological outcomes.
failureModes: One architecture and one seed per size limit generalization.
A compute-to-dollar estimate depends on hardware utilization and price assumptions.
The study does not measure wet-lab or real-world outcomes.
takeaways: Data filtering can constrain measured capability without making it impossible to relearn when weights and relevant data remain accessible.
lesson.scope: A visual summary of one ESM-2 study and its protein-task benchmarks, not a general biological risk assessment.

title: A schema is a shape, not a decision

lesson.summary: Use structured model output to parse a support decision, then validate its meaning before acting.
lesson.problem: Separate schema conformance from business validation.
objectives: Separate schema conformance from business validation.

walkthrough.title: Classify refund request
walkthrough.detail: The model proposes a refund classification for a user request.

walkthrough.title: Decision object
walkthrough.detail: The schema parser rejects malformed or incomplete output.

walkthrough.title: Parsed fields
walkthrough.detail: The policy check compares the proposal with trusted identity and order facts.

decisions: Treat a valid model object as a proposal until application checks pass.
failureModes: A schema-valid object can name an order the customer does not own.
A refusal or truncated response cannot be treated as an approval.
takeaways: Treat a valid model object as a proposal until application checks pass.

title: When a retrieved page gives orders

lesson.summary: Keep instructions in retrieved content from becoming tool authority.
lesson.problem: Identify the trust boundary between retrieved data and tool execution.
objectives: Identify the trust boundary between retrieved data and tool execution.

walkthrough.title: Ask for a summary
walkthrough.detail: The retriever fetches a page for a user summary request.

walkthrough.title: Fetch result
walkthrough.detail: The page may contain both relevant facts and an injected export instruction.

walkthrough.title: Content plus injected instruction
walkthrough.detail: The tool gate checks every proposed action against user authority and policy.

decisions: Authorize every tool action from the user and application policy, never a retrieved page.
failureModes: An injected page may cause an unauthorized export call before the final answer.
Keyword screening can miss paraphrased instructions.
takeaways: Authorize every tool action from the user and application policy, never a retrieved page.

title: Who can call this MCP tool?

lesson.summary: Trace identity from an MCP client to a protected resource and check permission per call.
lesson.problem: Separate protocol authorization from resource-level permission.
objectives: Separate protocol authorization from resource-level permission.

walkthrough.title: Request account lookup
walkthrough.detail: The client calls a protected server with a user token.

walkthrough.title: Call tool with token
walkthrough.detail: The server verifies the token and asks policy about the specific account.

walkthrough.title: Validate identity and action
walkthrough.detail: The authorized record returns through the server and client.

decisions: Verify identity, audience, scope, and resource ownership at the server.

A wrong-audience or expired token must not reach the resource.

title: Give a tool loop a stopping rule

lesson.summary: Set an iteration and elapsed-time budget for an agent before it starts calling tools.
lesson.problem: Design a stopping rule for repeated model and tool calls.
objectives: Design a stopping rule for repeated model and tool calls.

walkthrough.title: Ask for investigation
walkthrough.detail: The orchestrator starts a model run with a call and time budget.

walkthrough.title: Invoke with budget
walkthrough.detail: A model-proposed lookup returns a result or error to the orchestrator.

walkthrough.title: Request lookup
walkthrough.detail: The orchestrator continues only when the budget and progress rule allow it.

title: Before the agent retries a write

lesson.summary: Reconcile an uncertain write result before retrying an agent action.
lesson.problem: Distinguish a known failure from an unknown outcome after a timeout.
objectives: Distinguish a known failure from an unknown outcome after a timeout.

walkthrough.title: Propose order update
walkthrough.detail: The application sends an approved write with a stable operation key.

walkthrough.title: Write with operation key
walkthrough.detail: The remote API records its outcome even if the response is lost.

walkthrough.title: Record outcome
walkthrough.detail: After a timeout, the application reconciles the receipt before retrying.

decisions: Use a stable operation identity and verify the remote result before a retry.
failureModes: A blind retry can duplicate a side effect.
An unknown remote result requires reconciliation or intervention.
takeaways: Use a stable operation identity and verify the remote result before a retry.

title: When an agent chooses the analysis

lesson.summary: A randomized agent preference can shape analysis choices before a human makes the final recommendation.
lesson.problem: A final human sign-off may not independently check assumptions already shaped by an AI agent.
objectives: Trace how an agent's preference can affect analytic choices.
Distinguish a measured effect from what one study cannot establish.

walkthrough.title: Assign a lean
walkthrough.detail: A hidden coin flip gives the agent one of two defensible options at each choice.

walkthrough.title: Choose the analysis
walkthrough.detail: The agent argues its preference while the analyst chooses measurement and comparison assumptions.

walkthrough.title: Follow the result
walkthrough.detail: The choices shape an estimate before the analyst recommends an action.

decisions: Record the human's key assumptions before agent advice when independent judgment matters.
failureModes: Checking only the final arithmetic can miss an agent's influence on the analysis path.
A deliberately voiced preference in one fictional task does not estimate ordinary real-world deference.
takeaways: A human sign-off is not an independent check when the agent has already shaped the assumptions under review.
